newsitem.title: USA: Pentagon willing to review China shipyard deal.
newsitem.headline: Pentagon willing to review China shipyard deal.

text.p: U.S. Defense Secretary William Cohen said on Thursday he would be willing to review a deal to let a Chinese shipping company use part of the Long Beach Naval Shipyard in California if national security warranted it.

Responding to a letter from California Senators Dianne Feinstein and Barbara Boxer, Cohen told reporters, "Obviously, if there are any national security implications involved in this, we will review it."

Cohen, traveling to North Carolina with President Bill Clinton, said he understood the Long Beach navy base had gone through the U.S. base closure process and that "it was turned over to the city and the city made the determination to allow for this either sale or lease."

The California lawmakers raised questions about whether the use of part of the base as an expanded commercial port for the China Ocean Shipping Company (COSCO) might have implications for national security, and called for the Pentagon's analysis of the deal and Cohen's "personal views on the issue."
"The re-use plan submitted by the city of Long Beach to the Navy envisions a lease of former Long Beach Naval Shipyard facilities to COSCO for expanded cargo terminal facilities.
The local reuse authority expected the re-use plan would generate 900 to 1,600 jobs and wages worth $116 million, Boxer and Feinstein wrote.
"We would like to know if you feel there are any security reasons that this planned re-use should not occur," they wrote.
